newsitem.title: USA: America Online faces another user lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: America Online faces another user lawsuit.

text.p: America Online Inc is facing another lawsuit on behalf of subscribers that claim the company has not provided proper access to the Internet, two Seattle attorneys said in a statement.

The lawsuit, which seeks class-action status, was brought by Robert Hancock of Seattle, according to his attorneys Lynn Sarko and David Ashbaugh. This lawsuit joins at least three others that were filed on behalf of online subscribers.

On Thursday, America Online said it is spending more to upgrade its network to accommodate its eight million subscribers. The service will now spend $350 million to upgrade the network instead of the $250 million it had previously planned.
The company is also reducing its marketing activities, after the company introduced flat-rate pricing of $19.95 a month that has attracted a record number of members.
"AOL had to know that when they began offering the unlimited pricing plan that the demands on their system would skyrocket," Ashbaugh said in a statement.
